title: The amodale simon effect - does the auditive and visual simon effect demand different kinds of neuropsychological domains? Do digital medias take influence?
summary: Reaction times, incorrect reactions, omissions, processing times, number of correctly remembered numbers and words forwards and backwards should be recorded in order to find out whether the auditory and visual Simon effect differ in cognitive processing processes.
conditions: Reaction times, incorrect reactions, omitted reactions, total points on working memory tasks, processing time, cognitive flexibility

interventions.name: Recording reaction behavior as well as performance in terms of verbal and visual working memory and cognitive flexibility of healthy test subjects.

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
None
Exclusion criteria:
Limited and uncompensable visual acuity or hearing, motor limitations in the hands, underlying neurological or psychiatric illnesses
